deep.reconstruction:
This is the closing paragraph of E477, Euler's memoir on what are now called double zeta values (Euler sums). In Euler's notation p^k = Σ 1/x^k = ζ(k). The 'series of order λ' are sums of the type Σ_x x^{-m}(1 + 2^{-n} + … + x^{-n}), i.e. ζ(m,n) plus a single-zeta correction, of weight λ = m+n.

On the preceding page Euler gives the general closed form for odd weight λ. Each such sum is a rational combination of ζ(λ) and of products of the form ζ(2j)·ζ(λ−2j). This is the parity / reduction theorem for double zeta values of odd weight.

He then explains why his three methods fail for even weight, where the reductions run out at weight 8. In even weight, ζ(λ) and the products of even zetas are all rational multiples of π^λ, so any two of them can be compared. His methods therefore produce relations among these quantities rather than the determinations he needs.

This page finishes the thought: 'all the more remarkable, then, that in odd orders no assignable ratio whatever intervenes between the formulas p^λ, p^3, p^5, p^7 etc.' The point is that for odd weight the odd zeta values admit no such rational comparison, and yet the sums can be evaluated. He closes: 'Meanwhile there is no doubt that other methods exist by which series of even orders can be summed, even if the three set out here are by no means sufficient.'

In modern terms this contains two things:
(i) an implicit assertion that the odd zeta values ζ(3), ζ(5), ζ(7), … stand in no rational relation to one another or to the even zeta values. This is the irrationality and algebraic independence conjecture for odd zeta values.
(ii) a conjecture that all even-weight double sums reduce to single zeta values.
errors: Euler's closing conjecture is (conjecturally) false. Even-weight double zetas from weight 8 on are expected not to reduce to products of single zeta values. Weight 8 is exactly where Euler says his methods fail, and ζ(5,3) (equivalently ζ(6,2)) is the standard first irreducible double zeta. Irreducibility is unproven, but the Broadhurst–Kreimer and Zagier dimension conjectures and numerical evidence strongly support it.
Euler's claim that 'no ratio is assignable' between odd zeta values is stated as fact, not proved. It remains open apart from Apéry's ζ(3) and partial results such as Ball–Rivoal and Zudilin.

ideas.what: Explanation of the even-weight failure: relations among ζ(λ) and products ζ(2a)ζ(2b), which are all rational multiples of π^λ, use up the available equations.
ideas.modern_name: Counting of independent double shuffle relations in even weight
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E477); modern treatment by Borwein–Girgensohn, Zagier, and Gangl–Kaneko–Zagier

ideas.what: Implicit claim that odd zeta values have no rational relation among themselves or to even zetas.
ideas.modern_name: Irrationality / algebraic independence conjecture for ζ(2k+1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore conjecture; proven partial results by Apéry (1978), Ball–Rivoal (2001), Zudilin

ideas.what: Conjecture that even-weight double sums are summable by other methods.
ideas.modern_name: Reducibility of even-weight double zeta values (believed false from weight 8)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler; the counter-expectation is due to Broadhurst–Kreimer and Zagier

missed.claim: Euler explicitly juxtaposes the comparability of even zetas (rational multiples of π^λ) with the 'remarkable' absence of any assignable ratio among odd zetas. This is an early informal statement of the expected transcendence structure of zeta values. Modern MZV surveys usually cite E477 for the parity reduction, rarely for this remark.
missed.quote: Eo magis igitur est mirandum, quod in ordinibus imparibus nulla plane ratio assignabilis inter formulas p^λ, p^3, p^5, p^7 etc. intercedat.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical-priority nuance only. It shows Euler already linked the solvability of double sums to the (non)existence of relations among single zeta values, which is the core idea of the modern dimension conjectures.

deep.surprise_reason: E477 and its weight-8 obstruction are well known in the multiple zeta value literature (Borwein et al., Zagier, Sandifer). The remark about odd zetas lacking rational relations is a modest, mostly unemphasized historical detail, not a new result.
transcription_corrections: The superscripts after p^λ are small and hard to read; by context they are most plausibly the odd exponents 3, 5, 7, i.e. p^λ, p^3, p^5, p^7 etc. The [?] placeholders μ, ν, ξ are spurious.
